title: Joe's music career: saxophones and his Capitol records
summary: Joe began after she left home, played mainly alto, recorded Rocking Boogie and Mardi Gras for Capitol, and was a fine arranger.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And was he playing music back in Louisiana?

When I left home he was not playing music, no, he wasn't. He wasn't playing nor was my brother Charlie. I think I mentioned him, too. Charlie was a younger brother. Joe went into music after I left home, and he was very good. He almost was self taught, really, but he studied. He did do some studying, and he had a little group at home in Lake Charles, that is, and he played with little groups around

there, and finally, when he came out to California, then he got -- did manage to get in contact with some of the people that he knew, some of the musicians that he had met, and in their travels, you know, coming through Louisiana. And he did very, very well, and then he did do some things for Capitol on his own. "Rocking Boogie," was one, and he did a thing called, "Mardi Gras," and several other things that did very well. Well, he was somewhat ahead of his time, you know, because this was -- at that time it was before Rock and Roll, it wasn't even Rock and Roll, but it was a shuffle boogie type of thing. Most of his things were in that vein, you know, and something like the Louis Jordan shuffle rhythm type of thing. And he did very well.
But later something happened, I don't know, he just decided that he wanted to -- he didn't want to do it anymore. He just went into the religious vein.

We were all brought up religiously, you know. We were all Baptists, brought up in the Baptist church, in Lake Charles. But he got a little deeper into it and he just didn't -- he didn't want to stick with his jazz. I say unfortunately because he was so good at it. He's a marvelous musician, marvelous instrumentalist and a marvelous writer.
Joe played all the saxophones, didn't he?
Yes, he did. But his main instrument was the alto.
I remember seeing him play baritone. I remember alto and baritone more than tenor, but it seemed like he played all the saxophones. Did he play other instruments besides the saxophone?
He wrote. A marvelous writer, marvelous arranger. He could have made a living, or could still make a living today arranging if he wanted to do so, because he's just marvelous at it. But --
